task_instance: Run the SageMaker IAM preflight check (discover existing SageMaker execution roles, rank by last-used/created date, validate trust policy allows sagemaker.amazonaws.com, and only surface create-role guidance if none found) against an AWS account, as the skill's check_role.py is meant to do before deploying/training on SageMaker.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is querying a real AWS account's IAM state (iam:ListRoles, iam:GetRole, sts:GetCallerIdentity) to find/validate a usable SageMaker execution role. The skill source in this environment ships only SKILL.md + LICENSE -- scripts/check_role.py, scripts/create_role.py, references/trust-policy.json and references/minimum-permissions.json referenced by the doc are not actually present, so I reimplemented check_role.py's discover/rank/validate logic from the SKILL.md spec to test it. Running it for real requires AWS credentials: this runtime's environment only has placeholder values (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY='proxy-injected'), and `boto3 sts.get_caller_identity()` fails with InvalidClientTokenId, confirming there is no real AWS identity to preflight against. Per the safety rules I did not search for or supply real AWS credentials, and AWS IAM/SageMaker is an account-bound/potentially-paid service I should not use for real. I instead verified the reimplemented script's logic (regex role-name matching, last-used-then-created-date ranking, trust-policy validation, reject-on-missing-trust, reject-on-nonexistent-role) against a local moto-mocked IAM backend, and all assertions passed -- but this only proves the algorithm is sound, not that the skill's actual real-world deliverable (a preflight against the user's live AWS account) was accomplished, since no live account is reachable here.
evidence: Confirmed no usable AWS credentials: `python3 -c "import boto3; boto3.client('sts').get_caller_identity()"` -> ClientError('InvalidClientTokenId ... security token included in the request is invalid'). `which aws` -> not found (no AWS CLI binary in runtime either). Reimplemented scripts/check_role.py at /tmp/.../huggingface__skills__hf-cloud-sagemaker-iam-preflight/scripts/check_role.py implementing Step 1 (validate a named role) and Step 2 (discover + rank + validate) from SKILL.md. Wrote test_with_moto.py using moto's @mock_aws to create a mocked IAM with: a decoy role matching SageMaker naming but wrong (ec2.amazonaws.com) trust policy, an older valid AmazonSageMaker-ExecutionRole-*, a newer valid one, and an unrelated role. Ran in a venv (python3 -m venv venv; pip install boto3 moto[iam]) to avoid a system cryptography/cffi conflict. Output: discovery correctly excluded the unrelated role, ranking put the newest-created valid role first (moto never populates RoleLastUsed, exercising the create-date fallback path), the chosen ARN was the newest valid role (skipping the bad-trust decoy), explicit validation of the bad-trust role and a nonexistent role both correctly returned None/failure, and explicit validation of a good role returned its ARN. Printed 'ALL ASSERTIONS PASSED'. This demonstrates the algorithm works but not an actual completed preflight against a real AWS account, which the runtime cannot provide without credentials it is not permitted to obtain.
